title: Formal and informal issues: issue register or daily log
blurb: Decide whether an issue is handled formally in the issue register or informally in the daily log, and when an issue report is needed.
question: A supplier query is settled with a phone call, while a request to change an approved product needs the board's decision. Where should each be recorded?

teach.body: PRINCE2 7 gives issues two possible homes in the project log. Formal issues are recorded in the issue register. Informal issues, and sensitive matters where open access would be inappropriate, are recorded in the daily log. In plain English: if an issue needs formal handling, such as a decision by someone with authority or a change to a baseline, it goes on the register; if the project manager can simply deal with it, a diary note is enough.

root.label: Is it sensitive, unsuited to open access?

children.label: Does it need formal handling?
children.sub: a decision by others, a baseline change or formal review

children.label: Issue register
children.sub: plus an issue report where needed

children.label: Daily log
children.sub: the PM deals with it informally

teach.body: The issue register captures and maintains information on all formal issues, including an issue owner for each. Where an issue needs formal review, an issue report describes its impact on the project baseline, identifies ways to resolve it or address an off-specification, and recommends a decision. Issue reports are typically used for requests for change, off-specifications, business opportunities, and problems or concerns needing formal review.

teach.h: A formal issue from start to finish

teach.body: The daily log is the project manager's informal diary: informal issues, actions, notes and observations, plus sensitive issues. It is set up in starting up a project, so early issues and risks can be noted there before the registers are created in initiating a project. Using judgement matters: logging every trivial matter as a formal issue swamps decision-making, and some apparent issues are really risks.

items.label: Daily log set up; early issues and risks noted
Issue management approach written; issue register set up
Open issues get follow-on action; log closed

teach.body: Larchfield County Libraries is installing self-service kiosks. Project manager Nadia Rahman notes in the daily log that a supplier asked where to park the delivery van: she sorts it with one call. She also records there, privately, that a branch manager is struggling with personal pressures affecting the rollout. When senior user Patrick Doyle asks to add card payments to the approved kiosk design, Nadia enters it in the issue register and prepares an issue report for the change authority.

teach.text: Classic traps: the daily log is NOT the issue register; informal and sensitive issues go in the daily log, formal ones in the issue register. And an issue that can be handled within stage tolerance needs an issue report, not an exception report.

items: Formal issues: issue register, with an issue report where formal review is needed.
Informal issues and sensitive matters: daily log, the PM's informal diary.
The daily log is set up in starting up a project; the issue register in initiating a project.
Use judgement: too many trivial formal issues swamp decision-making.
Within stage tolerance: issue report, not exception report.

summary: You can now decide whether an issue belongs in the issue register (formal, with an issue report where formal review is needed) or the daily log (informal or sensitive). You can also say when each record is set up and why an issue within tolerance needs an issue report rather than an exception report.

A.q: Where should a formal issue be recorded?
A.why: Formal issues are captured and maintained in the issue register, part of the project log.

whyNot.0: The daily log is for informal and sensitive issues.
whyNot.2: The risk register holds uncertain events, not issues.
whyNot.3: The lessons log holds lessons, not issues.

A.q: A board member raises a sensitive personal matter that should not be visible to everyone who can read the registers. Where should the project manager record it?
A.why: Sensitive matters where open access would be inappropriate are recorded in the daily log.

whyNot.0: The issue register is open to those using the project log, which is unsuitable for a sensitive matter.
whyNot.1: A highlight report is circulated to the board and possibly other stakeholders, so it is not private.
whyNot.2: The lessons log records lessons for this and future projects, not sensitive issues.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The project manager records informal issues in the [?] log.
A.why: The daily log is the project manager's informal diary, where informal issues are recorded.

whyNot.2: There is no change log in PRINCE2 7; formal issues, including requests for change, go in the issue register.
whyNot.3: There is no quality log; the quality register records quality activities.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Every informal issue must be described in an issue report.
2. The daily log is set up in starting up a project.
3. Recording every trivial matter as a formal issue can swamp decision-making.
4. Sensitive issues are entered in the issue register so that everyone can see them.
B.why: The daily log is set up in starting up a project (2), and too many trivial formal issues swamp decision-making (3).

whyNot.0: Both are false: issue reports are for issues needing formal review, and sensitive issues go in the daily log.
whyNot.1: Statement 1 is false: informal issues are noted in the daily log without an issue report.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: sensitive issues go in the daily log.

B.q: A registered request for change needs a formal decision. Which product describes its impact on the baseline and recommends a decision?
B.why: An issue report describes an issue's impact on the project baseline, identifies ways to resolve it and recommends a decision.

whyNot.1: An exception report is for a forecast breach of stage or project tolerance.
whyNot.2: A highlight report summarizes stage status for the board at agreed intervals.
whyNot.3: A checkpoint report gives work package status from the team manager to the project manager.

B.q: The project manager settles a minor supplier query with a phone call. It needs no decision from anyone else and no baseline change. Where is it best recorded?
B.why: An issue the project manager can deal with informally is noted in the daily log.

whyNot.0: The issue register is for formal issues; this one needs no formal handling.
whyNot.1: An issue report is for issues needing formal review and a recommended decision.
whyNot.3: No tolerance breach is forecast, so there is no exception.

C.q: A team manager reports an off-specification that can be handled within stage tolerance but needs a formal decision. Where is it recorded, and which report is prepared?
C.why: An off-specification needing a formal decision is a formal issue for the issue register, and within tolerance it is described in an issue report, not an exception report.

whyNot.0: It needs formal handling, so it belongs in the issue register, and within tolerance there is no exception.
whyNot.1: An off-specification is an issue, not a risk.
whyNot.3: No stage tolerance breach is forecast, so an exception report is not needed.

C.q: During starting up a project, before any registers exist, a concern is raised. Where is it noted, and when is the issue register set up?
options: In the daily log; the register is set up in initiating a project
In the lessons log; the register is set up in controlling a stage
In the project brief; the register is set up at a stage boundary
In the risk register; the register is set up in directing a project
C.why: The daily log is set up in starting up a project and holds early issues and risks; the issue register is set up in initiating a project alongside the issue management approach.

whyNot.1: The lessons log holds lessons, and the issue register exists before delivery stages begin.
whyNot.2: The project brief is not a record of issues, and the register is set up in initiation.
whyNot.3: The risk register does not exist yet either, and registers are set up by the PM in initiation, not by the board.

C.q: Which statement about formal and informal issues is correct?
options: Formal issues go in the daily log; informal ones in the issue register
Formal issues go in the issue register; informal ones in the daily log
Both go in the issue register, with informal ones marked as minor
Both go in the lessons log until the project board has reviewed them
C.why: Formal issues are recorded in the issue register; informal issues, and sensitive ones, go in the daily log.

whyNot.2: Informal issues are kept out of the register so it is not swamped by trivial matters.
whyNot.3: The lessons log holds lessons, not issues awaiting review.

reteach.title: The head teacher's two books
reteach.question: Which of a head teacher's concerns go in the formal incident book, and which in her own notebook?

blocks.body: A head teacher keeps a formal incident book for anything that needs a governors' decision or an official record: a broken fire door, a request to change the timetable. Small things she sorts herself (a missing box of pens) and confidential matters (a colleague's family illness) go in her own notebook. Writing every missing pen in the incident book would bury the things that matter.

blocks.text: Formal handling means the issue register. Informal or sensitive means the daily log.

explain.body: The daily log is the project manager's informal diary: informal issues, actions, notes and observations, and sensitive issues.

options: A record of all quality activities and their results
A list of all products in a plan and their status
The PM's informal diary of issues, actions and notes
An informal repository of lessons for later use
test.why: The daily log is the project manager's informal diary of informal issues, actions, notes and observations.

explain.h: When an issue report is used
explain.body: Issue reports are typically used for requests for change, off-specifications, business opportunities, and problems or concerns that need formal review.

test.q: Which kinds of issue are typically described in an issue report?
options: Lessons and observations from the daily log
Risks that exceed the project risk tolerance
Products that are waiting for a quality review
test.why: Issue reports are typically used for requests for change, off-specifications, business opportunities, and problems or concerns needing formal review.

whyNot.1: Lessons and observations are not issues needing formal review.
whyNot.2: Risks are handled through the risk practice and risk register.
whyNot.3: Products awaiting review are tracked through quality planning and the quality register.

explain.body: Some issues should not be visible to everyone with access to the registers. These sensitive matters are recorded in the daily log.

test.q: Why might the project manager record an issue in the daily log rather than the issue register?
options: It has already happened and is certain to continue
It needs a formal decision from the project board
It is a request to change a baselined product
It is sensitive, and open access would be unsuitable
test.why: Sensitive matters where open access would be inappropriate are recorded in the daily log.

whyNot.0: Having happened makes it an issue, not a risk; it says nothing about formal or informal handling.
whyNot.1: Needing a formal board decision makes it a formal issue for the issue register.
whyNot.2: A request for change goes through change control as a formal issue.

explain.body: If an issue can be handled within stage tolerance, it is described in an issue report. An exception report is needed only when a stage or project tolerance breach is forecast.

test.q: An issue needs a formal decision, but its impact stays within stage tolerance. Which report should be prepared?
test.why: Within tolerance, the issue is described in an issue report; no exception report is needed.

whyNot.0: An exception report is for a forecast breach of stage or project tolerance.
whyNot.2: An end stage report is produced at the end of a stage to support the next decision.
whyNot.3: A highlight report gives regular stage status; it is not where an issue's options and recommendation are set out.
